cases.label: Map the tissue
cases.question: You need to inspect how cellular regions relate to trabeculae, adipocytes and sinusoids. Which preparation best answers that question?
cases.reason: The intact spatial relationships are the target. A smear disperses cells and cannot preserve the same architectural map.

cases.label: Read circulating cells
cases.question: You need to compare nuclear lobation and granule appearance among circulating leukocytes. Which preparation best answers that question?
cases.reason: A well-spread blood film samples circulating cells and supports comparison of individual nuclear and cytoplasmic features.

cases.label: Compare developing cells
cases.question: You need to compare chromatin and cytoplasm across a marrow maturation series. Which preparation best answers that question?
cases.reason: A well-preserved aspirate spreads developing cells for detailed morphology. A tissue section gives complementary architecture.
